report_text: Patient admitted to ICU with septic shock requiring ventilator support and vasopressors.
Complex case with multiple comorbidities; surgery planned; poorly controlled diabetes.
Uncomplicated urinary tract infection, responding to oral antibiotics, no ICU care.
70yo male with acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction, awaiting emergency cardiac catheterization.
45yo female with mild asthma exacerbation, O2 saturation 98% on room air, discharged with albuterol inhaler.
Patient with acute kidney injury secondary to dehydration, creatinine 2.5 mg/dL, starting IV fluids.
Neutropenic fever in a 55yo oncology patient post-chemotherapy, admitted for broad-spectrum IV antibiotics.
Routine follow-up for well-controlled primary hypertension, BP 120/80, no new complaints.
Extensive acute pulmonary embolism with right heart strain on echo, stable blood pressure.
Type 2 diabetes with newly diagnosed microalbuminuria, initiating ACE inhibitor therapy.
22yo with acute appendicitis, localized pain, stable vitals, prepped for laparoscopic appendectomy.
Elderly patient with severe community-acquired pneumonia, confusion, RR 30, requiring high-flow nasal cannula.
Minor laceration on left forearm, closed with sutures, no sign of infection.
Acute upper GI bleed with melena and tachycardia, hemoglobin dropped to 6.8 g/dL, planning EGD.

Patient presenting with subjective fever and viral URI symptoms, chest X-ray clear, normal vitals.

Subarachnoid hemorrhage with altered mental status, admitted to neuro ICU.
